_comment: Which score a module gets, keyed on its taxonomy SUBCATEGORY.
A module may override any of this with a preview.json in its own repo.
`audio: null` means NO AUDIO PREVIEW, deliberately -- streaming, live-input,
assistant and tuner modules have nothing deterministic to render, and a
synthesised clip for them would be a fabrication rather than a preview.

`adaptive_density` spreads the phrase to suit each PRESET's measured release. The score fires a note every ~0.28 s and releases across the fleet run 0.00-3.40 s, so without it a long-release preset stacks a dozen voices and turns to mud.
`_by_tag` overrides the subcategory rule for a module carrying that tag.

mono-bass._why: A bass patch previewed in the treble is a preview of the wrong instrument. The octave fit puts note 60 where note 60 belongs; this then moves the PHRASE down an octave, which is a musical decision the fit cannot make.

drum-machine._why: A drum machine is played on its own voices, not on a melodic line; the score is built from the module's declared voices at render time.

_all._why: An FX is previewed on a real instrument playing the same phrase every other module plays, so effects are comparable with each other and with the synths. The source is chosen by MEASUREMENT, not taste: wurl renders C4 at 262.5 Hz with tight pitch and a +27.2 dB attack. The previous source (obxd, default preset) rendered at 525 Hz -- an octave high -- with a +11.7 dB attack and a detuned unison that smears whatever the effect does. A slow-attack pad is worse still: hera's Strings 1 is in tune and has -3.5 dB of attack, so a reverb has nothing to excite it. Dry/wet goes to 50% OF THE RANGE THE MODULE DECLARES.
Driven into ONE reference instrument, the same one the audio FX use, so a preview that changes means the MIDI FX changed.

tuner-analysis._why: nothing to render without an input

assistant._why: needs an API key and a person

_all._why: An overtake module owns the whole surface and is not fed MIDI from a slot; there is no score that means anything.

bass._why: Applies to a bass patch that is NOT in the Mono & Bass subcategory -- tb3po is a tool, and a bass preset can live inside a polysynth. A tag rule overrides the subcategory's, and stacks with nothing: transpose is set, not accumulated.
